             Rules of Conduct for Planning Commission Meetings
PROCEDURE FOR PUBLIC COMMENT

1.   Any person or entity may appear in person or be represented by an authorized agent at any meeting of the
     Commission.

2.   Unless altered by the Chair, the order of the procedure on an application shall be:

     a. The supporting agency staff will introduce the application, including staff’s recommendations and a
        summary of pertinent written comments and reports concerning the application

     b. The applicant will be allowed up to 15 minutes to make their presentation.

     c. The Community Council representative can present their comments as applicable.

     d. Where applicable, persons in favor of, or not opposed to, the application will be invited to speak.

     e. Where applicable, persons opposing the application, in whole or in part will be invited to speak.

     f. Where applicable, the applicant will be allowed 5 minutes to provide concluding statements.

     g. Surrebuttals may be allowed at the discretion of the Chair.

CONDUCT FOR APPLICANTS AND THE PUBLIC

1.   Speakers will be called to the podium by the Chair.

2.   Each speaker, before talking, shall give his or her name and address.

3.   All comments should be directed to the Commissioners, not to the staff or to members of the audience.

4.   For items where there are several people wishing to speak, the Chair may impose a time limit, usually 3
     minutes per person, or 5 minutes for a group spokesperson. If a time limit is imposed on any member or
     spokesperson of the public, then the same time limit is imposed on other members or spokespersons of the
     public, respectively.

5.   Unless otherwise allowed by the Chair, no questions shall be asked by the speaker or Commission Members.

6.   Only one speaker is permitted before the Commission at a time.

7.   The discussion must be confined to essential points stated in the application bearing on the desirability or
     undesirability of the application.

8.   The Chair may cease any presentation or information that has already been presented and acknowledge that it
     has been noted in the public record.

9.   No personal attacks shall be indulged in by either side, and such action shall be sufficient cause for stopping the
     speaker from proceeding.

10. No applause or public outbursts shall be permitted.

11. The Chair or supporting agency staff may request police support to remove offending individuals who refuse to
    abide by these rules.

12. After the public comment portion of a meeting or hearing has concluded, the discussion will be limited to the
    Planning Commission and Staff.

Request: Preliminary Plat Approval

Planner: Shad Cook
Planning Staff Recommendation: Approve with Conditions
Applicant Name: Korey Kinder (for D.R. Horton)




                                        PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The applicant, D.R. Horton, is requesting approval of the Gateway to Little Valley Phase 4 preliminary plat. The
subject property is 18.01 acres in size and is zoned P-C. The phase includes 30 Single-Family style homes and 173
Townhome units. This project is a part of the Gateway to Little Valley planned community. Development
standards for this project are contained in the P-C zoning ordinance and the October 2018 Master Development
Agreement between Magna, D.R. Horton, Kennecott, and the Granite School District.




                                   SITE & VICINITY DESCRIPTION
The property is located west of 8400 West and spans from approximately 3600 S to 4000 S. The project is
surrounded mostly by residential zoning, but there is also a manufacturing zone in the area to the north and
west. The southern portion of this phase is adjacent to the proposed location for the new Cyprus High School. As
a part of the Gateway to Little Valley development, a variety of residential densities will surround the project
area. The development project has an average density of nine dwelling units per acre.
        Request: Subdivision                                                     File #: PUD2021-000596




                                 GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS
Planning Area 4

General Plan Recommendation: Gateway to Little Valley Development

The Magna General Plan was adopted in 2021. The Gateway to Little Valley project was significant enough to
include in the General Plan. The general plan describes this development as a 145-acre, 1,360 unit project with a
mix of housing types, densities, open space, infrastructure, and amenities. The development represents
significant growth in Magna.

                                     PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

18.08.010 - Procedure generally.
The planning commission shall be the land use authority for subdivisions. In order to assure that each
subdivision fully complies with the provisions of this title, the director or director's designee shall administer
formal application and review procedures for subdivisions. An application shall not be deemed complete until
the full application, fees and all required materials have been submitted. The payment of a partial fee and
submission of preliminary plans for a pre-submittal review does not constitute a complete application.
Each process shall include the following components:
         A. An application procedure, which shall include:
                  1. Submission of an application form, as designed by the director or director's designee to
                  clearly indicate the type of application, property address, applicant information, and other
                  pertinent information;
                  2. Submission of supplementary materials, including a legal description, property plat, the
                  required number of plans/preliminary plats, and mailing labels (if required) for notifications;
                  3. Payment of fees, as required under Title 3, Revenue and Finance.
         B. A review procedure, which shall include:
                  1. An on-site review by the director or director's designee as provided by Utah Code 17-27a-303;
                  2. Review of the submitted site plan/preliminary plat for compliance with Magna land use
                  ordinances;
                  3. Reference of the application and site plan/preliminary plat to any other government agency
                  and/or affected entity which the director or director's designee deems necessary to protect the
                  health, safety, and welfare of the public and to ensure the project's compliance with all
                  applicable ordinances and codes;
                  4. The processing of any exception requests that have been made in conjunction with the
                  subdivision application.
         C. A preliminary plat approval procedure, which shall include:
                  1. Confirmation that all necessary agencies have responded to the requests for
                  recommendation with a recommendation of approval or approval with conditions;
                  2. Integration of the recommendations from the other government agencies and affected
                  entities involved above into the preliminary plat;
                  3. Receipt of a recommendation from the planning staff;
                  4. Approval of the preliminary plat as outlined in Section 18.12.030, and issuing a preliminary
                  plat approval letter.

Subdivision Summary                                                                                     Page 4 of 5
        Request: Subdivision                                                     File #: PUD2021-000596

       D. A final plat approval procedure, which shall include:
                1. An engineering review to ensure that the final plat complies with all conditions of approval of
                the preliminary plat and to ensure that the final plat complies with the design standards, codes,
                and ordinances and with minimum engineering/surveying requirements;
                2. A check of appropriate background information, such as: lot access, property title, record of
                survey, field boundary verification, etc.;
                3. The collection of the necessary approval signatures (planning commission representative,
                director or director's designee, health department, attorney, Magna mayor or their designees)
                on the final plat;
                4. Payment of final fees and bond;
                5. Recordation of the plat.



                               PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION
The MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning Commission approve the Preliminary Plat for
Gateway to Little Valley Phase 4 subject to the following conditions:

   1. That the applicant work with MSD staff and outside review agencies to comply with the final plat
      procedure prior to plat recordation.

   2. That the applicant pay any fees or post a bond to guarantee improvements prior to subdivision plat
      recordation.

Request: Subdivision
Applicant Name: Ron Larsen

MSD Planner: Morgan Julian
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval with Conditions



 SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

 The applicant is requesting a subdivision on a half-acre (.5) lot. The lot in question is located directly south of 3100
 S. The lot is zoned R-2-6.5 (Medium Density Residential). It is surrounded by residential uses East, West, North and
 South. Parcels directly North of the lot in questioned are zoned A-1/zc (See Figure 1).




                                                        N
                                                                                                              N
        Figure 1: Zoning Map of the Neighborhood                       Figure 1a: Aerial View of Property
             Planning & Development Services • 2001 South State Street, N3-600 • Salt Lake City, Utah 84190
Request: Subdivision                                                                      File #: SUB2021-000488

PROJECT & BACKGROUND DESCRIPTION

The proposed subdivision will divide the existing lot into two distinct lots (see Attachment 2). It is currently
occupied by a single-family home and will remain on the west lot in the proposed subdivision.


PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

No issues of concern are identified at this time (see Attachment 1). All agency reviewers have given an “ok” to the
conceptual review with additional information and revisions being required for technical review and final approval.

      Zoning Considerations:
      The proposed lots 1 and 2 will comply with the minimum lot area of 6,000 square feet and width of 60 feet
      for the R-2-6.5 zone. Lot 1 will have an area of 13,467 sq. ft and Lot 2 will have an area of 8,112 sq. ft. This
      will exceed the minimum lot area for any main dwelling type allowed in the zone. Lot 1 will meet the
      minimum lot width with 103’. Lot 2 will meet the minimum lot width 62’ (see Attachment 2).

      The existing house on Lot 1 will still meet the setback requirements of the R-2-6.5 after the parcel is
      subdivided.

PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Metro Township Planning
Commission grant Preliminary Approval for Subdivision with the following conditions:

  1. The applicant shall comply with all requirements from other reviewing agencies prior to final approval.

                                            Files # CUP2021-000421

                                      Conditional Use Summary

Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: August 11, 2022
Parcel ID: 14-21-200-033-0000
Current Zone: M-2/zc
Property Address: 2360 S 7200 W
Request: Conditional Use for a lay down yard that will include tracked equipment
Applicant Name: Derrick Hacking

MSD Planner: Justin Smith
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Planning Commission Approval


PROJECT SUMMARY

The applicant is applying for a conditional use for the purpose of a laydown yard in Magna. The laydown yard
will be used to store equipment related to construction and will include tracked equipment. The project will
include a temporary building and will include a slated privacy chainlink fence around the property. The
temporary building is 5,000 square feet in size and will be used to store equipment out of view and out of the
elements. The temporary building is uninhabitable and is intended to be used as a living or office space.

The applicant has stated that this site will not be used for the storage of structure-like materials such as shipping
containers.

SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

The property is currently vacant and is zoned M-2/zc. The M-2/zc zone is intended to provide areas in the
county for heavy industrial uses. The M-2/zc zone allows for a laydown yard as a conditional use. The property
to the north is vacant and is zoned M-1. The property the east, across 7200 W, is a truck dealership that is within
West Valley City city limits. The property to the south, across SR-201, is zoned C-2/zc and is currently used for a
gas station. The property the west is zoned A-20 and is used as a residence according to the assessor’s office.
        Request: Conditional Use                                                   File #: CUP2021-000421




GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS

Utah State Law (Ch. 17-27a-405) identifies General Plans as advisory guides for land use decisions. The Magna
General Plan was adopted in 2021 and shows this property as an Industrial / Employment Development Area.
The Industrial/Employment Development Area is intended to provide an area. This property is also located in
the North Magna Industrial Catalyst Area which is an industrial in Magna along 2400 S that extends northward
and is next to the proposed location of the Inland Port.

The WFRC 2040 Plan shows a wider right-of-way for the 2400 S and the landowner has agreed to dedicate the
land to acquire the conditional use.

ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION

A few issues of concern are identified at this time. Engineering requires that the dedication be recorded, but has
not been reviewed by the Salt Lake County Surveyor’s Department. Engineering requires minor revisions regarding
traffic and hydrology. Engineering has stated that infrastructure improvements are required, but that a delay
agreement could be acquired if the party desires. Additional storm drain components on the grading and drainage
plan and relating to the storm water calculations are required from Engineering. Planning requires a landscape
plan as part of the conditional use. Those agencies require additional information for a conceptual approval. A
few agencies have revisions being required for technical review and final approval.




Conditional Use Summary                                                                                Page 2 of 4
        Request: Conditional Use                                                     File #: CUP2021-000421



PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

The M-2/zc zone allows for a laydown yard, or contractor’s yard, as a conditional use. In order to get a conditional
use the applicant must receive approval from the Planning Commission.

Chapter 19.77.020 states that the interior of equipment storage yards have an exemption from the provisions of
the landscaping requirements. The exterior of the lot does require landscaping for the front yard. The
requirements are laid out in Chapter 19.77 and may not require vegetation, but may allow for xeriscaping. No
landscape plan has been submitted. Infrastructure improvements would still be required along the roadway,
unless a delay agreement is accepted. The applicant can receive delay agreements from the Planning Commission
with the recommendation from Engineering.

Chapter 19.80 does not state any specific parking requirement for a laydown yard and vehicles will be stored
hidden from view. For any parking on-site, the parking lot finish must have a dust free surface that is approved by
Engineering.

MSD staff has reviewed the application and has found that the development proposal with staff recommendations
is consistent with the surrounding land uses. Full compliance with required ordinances and policies will be verified
through the subsequent technical review process before the issuance of the Land Use permit, and furthermore
through the building permit review and inspection process. Staff finds that the plan meets, or will meet with
conditions, all required standards of the ordinance necessary for preliminary approval by the Planning
Commission.

PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning
Commission grant approval for the conditional use for a car wash and soda shop with the following
conditions:

    1. The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the M-2/zc Zone.
    2. The applicant be required to comply with the requirements from all reviewing agencies.
    3. The applicant be required to comply with the Landscape Code requirements and have the
        improvements bonded prior to operation.
    4. The applicant be required to acquire a business license prior to operation.
    5. The applicant be required to have the deed of warranty and ROW dedication be reviewed by the Salt
        Lake County Surveyor’s Office and be recorded and executed.
    6. The applicant be required to provide curb, gutter, and sidewalk along the property line that abuts any
        public road or right-of-way or acquire a delay agreement.
    7. The storage of shipping containers on the site is prohibited.
    8. Parking areas must have a dust free surface approved by Engineering, subject to Magna Code, Section
        19.80.030.
    9. All vehicle repair is prohibited on site and vehicles, trailers, and equipment located on the property
        must be operable.
    10. All equipment storage must be setback 40 feet from public roads.
    11. The applicant be required to comply with any applicable off-street parking requirements.

                                           Files # CUP2022-000556

                                     Conditional Use Summary

Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: August 11, 2022
Parcel ID: 14-29-127-042-0000
Current Zone: C-2
Property Address: 8426 W Washakie
Request: Conditional Use for a Car Wash and Soda Shop
Applicant Name: Quin Denning

MSD Planner: Justin Smith
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Planning Commission Approval


PROJECT SUMMARY

The applicant is applying for a conditional use for the purpose of opening a car wash and a drive thru soda shop.
The car wash is an automatic car wash that has a drive thru soda shop and vacuums. This property is located in
the Flangas Crossing PUD, a development plan that includes the Oquirrh Hills Apartments, a Burger King, a
Family Dollar, and a few other businesses.

SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

The location of the proposed conditional use is currently vacant and is zoned C-2. The C-2 zone is intended to
provide areas in the county for community commercial development. The C-2 zone allows car washes as a
conditional use. The property to the north is currently vacant is also zoned C-2. The property the east across
8400 W is zoned R-4-8.5 and is currently being used for single family housing. The property to the south across
Washakie Lane is zoned C-2 and is currently vacant. The property the west is zoned C-2 and is currently being
used for an apartment complex.
        Request: Conditional Use                                                   File #: CUP2022-000556




PROJECT BACKGROUND AND DESCRIPTION

The proposed car wash and soda shop is proposed on Lot 3 of the Flangas Crossing PUD. This lot sits on the
northwest corner of the intersection of 8400 West and Washakie Lane. Access will be provided through
Washakie Lane by way of a pre-existing curb return.

GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS

Utah State Law (Ch. 17-27a-405) identifies General Plans as advisory guides for land use decisions. The Magna
General Plan was adopted in 2021 and shows this property as a Neighborhood Stabilization Area. The
Neighborhood Stabilization Area future land use designation is intended to preserve the historic character of the
area while addressing gaps in infrastructure and property maintenance. The Neighborhood Stabilization Area
prohibits industrial areas as well as large format commercial that is greater than 20,000 square feet. The
prohibition of large format commercial is intended for big box stores and would not prohibit a car wash from
being in the Neighborhood Stabilization Area.

Flangas Crossing PUD is designated as a catalytic area in Magna. Catalytic area’s are parts of Magna that deemed
to be critical to the future of Magna. The Flangas Crossing PUD area is seen as being an extension of magna
Main StreetThe proposed project will be a new commercial use at this commercial node that is an extension of
Magna Main Street.

Conditional Use Summary                                                                                Page 2 of 4
          Request: Conditional Use                                                   File #: CUP2022-000556

ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION

No issues of concern are identified at this time. All agency reviewers have given an “ok” to the conceptual review
with additional information and revisions being required for technical review and final approval.


PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

The C-2 zone is intended for commercial development and allows for a car wash as a conditional use. This project
meets the require setbacks as determined by both the C-2 zone and the Flangas Crossing PUD. The Flangas
Crossing PUD was approved with conditions. One of these conditions is that the development of any lot within
the PUD requires a separate PUD approval. This site plan and conditional use approval fulfills that PUD
requirement. The second requirement of this PUD is a setback between 20 and 25 feet.

Parking

A car wash and soda shop combination does not have a minimum parking requirement, but 10 parking spots
have been provided as part of the conditional use for any employees on shift and customers for the soda shop.
In addition to those 10 spots, the applicant is providing 19 free vacuum parking stalls.

Landscaping

A Landscaping Plan is required as part of the conditional use review process. Landscaping is required at the ends
of rows of parking with a minimum of a eight foot wide planter at the end of each end of a row of parking. There
are additional landscaping requirements for encroaching within fifteen feet of the neighboring parcel. The
applicant would be required to provide a decorate fence on the interior side of the landscaped area, or a
continuous hedge may be provided. The area of land between the parcels should be graded to a maximum slope
of 3:1 of up to thirty-two inches in height. To encroach within fifteen feet, the applicant is required to have a
horizontally and vertically articulated decorative wall along the interior edge of the yard or setback area. Due to
the tight nature of this lot, the distance between the curb face of the on-site parking and the curb face and
covered parking of the apartment complex is being treated as the distance between the parking and property
line. The apartment has a stretch of garages that run parallel to the property line with the car wash and can help
serve as a barrier to light and sound.

Signage

A formal sign package must be submitted as part of the review process. The applicant has yet to submit any type
of sign plan, but any submitted sign plan must meet the requirements that are laid out in Chapter 19.82.

Review Criteria

The Planning Commission is the decision making body for conditional use permits. If approval is granted for this
conditional use then the projet will advance into the technical review phase who will then review the project
based on compliance with the code.

MSD staff has reviewed the application and has found that the development proposal with staff recommendations
is consistent with the surrounding land uses. Full compliance with required ordinances and policies will be verified
through the subsequent technical review process before the issuance of the Land Use permit, and furthermore
through the building permit review and inspection process. Staff finds that the plan meets, or will meet with
conditions, all required standards of the ordinance necessary for preliminary approval by the Planning
Commission.

Conditional Use Summary                                                                                  Page 3 of 4
        Request: Conditional Use                                               File #: CUP2022-000556



PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Magna Planning
Commission grant approval for the conditional use for a car wash and soda shop with the following
conditions:

   1.   The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the C-2 Zone.
   2.   The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the Flangas PUD.
   3.   The applicant be required to comply with the requirements from all reviewing agencies.
   4.   The applicant be required to comply with the Landscape code requirements.
   5.   The applicant be required to comply with the Sign code requirements.
   6.   The applicant be required to comply with off-street parking requirements.

ATTACHMENTS:
   A. Site Plan
   B. Elevations
   C. Flangas Crossing PUD

                                           Files # CUP2022-000624

                                     Conditional Use Summary


Public Body: Magna Planning Commission
Meeting Date: August 11, 2022
Parcel ID: 14-21-302-001-0000
Current Zone: M-1/zc
Property Address: 2490 S 7600 W
Request: Conditional Use for a Parking Addition
Applicant Name: Logan Terry

MSD Planner: Justin Smith
MSD Planning Staff Recommendation: Planning Commission Approval


PROJECT SUMMARY

The applicant is applying for a conditional use for the purpose of adding a parking addition to the Fedex truck
terminal in Magna.

SITE & ZONE DESCRIPTION

The location of the proposed conditional use is currently vacant and is zoned M-1/zc. The property is currently
the location of a Fedex truck terminal. Parking was included with the terminal, but this section of parking is
being added separately. The proposed parking addition is on the west side of the lot that it shares with the
trucking terminal.
        Request: Conditional Use                                                   File #: CUP2022-000624




GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS

Utah State Law (Ch. 17-27a-405) identifies General Plans as advisory guides for land use decisions. The Magna
General Plan was adopted in 2021 and calls for this location to be for Industrial and Economic Development. The
truck terminal serve as economic development and provide jobs to residents in the area. This parking addition
would serve a purpose that is industrial and economic development in nature as it would provide parking for
employees at the terminal. The parking area is being created serve the facility and, as such, is being used in a
manner that is consistent with the General Plan’s call for Industrial and Economic Development on this parcel.

ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION

No issues of concern are identified at this time. All agency reviewers have given an “ok” to the conceptual review
with additional information and revisions being required for technical review and final approval.




Conditional Use Summary                                                                                Page 2 of 3
        Request: Conditional Use                                                      File #: CUP2022-000624

PLANNING STAFF ANALYSIS

This parking lot is to serve the Fedex facility that already exists on site. This part of the project was pushed back
in order to meet the original deadlines for the truck terminal. The existing site has parking and landscaping already
on site and this parking addition will expand upon that. The M-1 zone is intended for light industrial uses and
allows for a parking lot as a permitted use, but this parking lot is coming as a conditional use since it is part of a
trucking terminal which is allowed in the M-1 zone as conditional use.

MSD staff has reviewed the application and has found that the development proposal with staff recommendations
is consistent with the surrounding land uses. Full compliance with required ordinances and policies will be verified
through the subsequent technical review process before the issuance of the Land Use permit, and furthermore
through the building permit review and inspection process. Staff finds that the plan meets, or will meet with
conditions, all required standards of the ordinance necessary for preliminary approval by the Planning
Commission.

PLANNING STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based on the findings stated above, the MSD Planning Staff recommends that the Salt Lake County Planning
Commission grant approval for the conditional use for the parking lot expansion with the following
conditions:

    1. The applicant be required to comply with the requirements of the M-1/zc zone.
    2. The applicant be required to comply with the requirements from all reviewing agencies.
    3. The applicant be required to comply with the Landscape code requirements.

ATTACHMENTS:
   A. Site Plan
   B. Landscape Plan
